A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WebDancer research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original WebDancer benchmark results, data and training ablations, consistency analyses, and a memorization experiment in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original WebDancer evaluations and analyses, including results on GAIA, WebWalkerQA, and the BrowseComp benchmarks.

M1.justification: The CRAWLQA/E2HQA construction procedures, trajectory sampling and filtering, ReAct tools, masked SFT loss, and DAPO training remain unchanged. Figure 1's new annotations illustrate the existing procedure rather than introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CRAWLQA, E2HQA, and the same open-only QA sources. Evaluation coverage remains GAIA, WebWalkerQA, BrowseComp, and BrowseComp-zh; no task, language, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership, including Search-o1, R1-Searcher, WebThinker-Base/RL, SimpleDS, OpenAI DR, and Vanilla ReAct. Appendix E.2 preserves the baseline descriptions.

E3.justification: Both use 103 GAIA text-only validation questions and 680 WebWalkerQA test questions, with the same metrics, model configurations, and evaluation procedures. Appendix E.3 retains the inference settings and RL rollout configuration.

E4.justification: Figures 3–5 and Table 3 retain the data-efficiency, filtering, SFT/RL, CoT-transfer, training-step, and temperature analyses. The 69-trajectory memorization experiment and Appendix F's case study are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both describe three independent attempts for the Pass@3/Cons@3 analysis. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The tables and plotted results match. For example, QwQ-32B WebDancer retains Table 1 averages of 51.5 on GAIA and 47.9 on WebWalkerQA; Table 2 retains BrowseComp results of 3.8/7.9 and BrowseComp-zh results of 18.0/31.5.

T1.justification: The trajectory formulation, SFT loss, DAPO objective, advantage calculation, and reward equations remain mathematically equivalent. No theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same four-stage agent-building contribution and claims about the effectiveness of data synthesis followed by SFT and on-policy RL. The claimed scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same interpretations of filtering, cold-start SFT, reasoning transfer, RL benefits, and web-environment instability. Appendix A preserves the limitations concerning tools, task generalization, data utilization, rollout cost, and thinking patterns.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E retain the data statistics, filtering thresholds, prompts, software, model settings, and hardware information. The existing repository URL moves to the title block; v3 does not explicitly establish a change in resource availability.

R1.justification: All 72 referenced works are retained. Section 6 and Appendix C preserve the same positioning relative to prior agents, including WebThinker and SimpleDeepSearcher; reference reordering and author–year formatting do not change that positioning.

P1.justification: The prose and section sequence remain nearly verbatim. v3 changes citation style, alphabetizes the bibliography, and revises title-page and contact material. The citation conversion also introduces a malformed 'Zheng et al. (2025;?)' reference in Section 6.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns the document with a boxed abstract, colored headings, different typography, and wider text layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with crawl-depth and entity-replacement labels; retained figures, tables, prompts, and case-study boxes are resized or reflowed throughout.

improvement.justification: Figure 1 more explicitly connects crawl depth and successive entity replacements to the unchanged data-generation method, and Figure 6's prompt now fits on one page. These provide modest clarity gains. The malformed Section 6 citation and Figure 8's final answer being stranded on a separate page reduce the polish; scientific evidence and reproducibility remain unchanged.
